why: TWO PACKAGES, ONE SCRIPT NAME, DIFFERENT BODIES — the shape that decides how `scriptsDeTodos` may return its answer. The root of the workspace declares `format` rewriting everything; `apps/web` declares `format` checking. Collecting the scripts into a map keyed by NAME loses one of the two bodies, and it loses the one read first: git lists `apps/web/package.json` before `package.json`, so the root’s writer overwrites the package’s checker and the rule accuses a repository that gates. That is why the helper returns PAIRS. The `fail` side is the same two packages with both `format` scripts rewriting — the collision is still there, and now nothing checks, so it must fail. Between them, the pair pins that the rule reads EVERY body and not one per name.
